Updates `postcss` from 8.5.15 to 8.5.28
Release notes

Sourced from postcss's releases.

8.5.28

  • Fixes types regression.

8.5.27

  • Fixed removing any comments starting with /*# (by @​dylanpulver).
  • Fixed * hack before a comment in Custom Properties (by @​Jaybhade).
  • Fixed empty values in the middle of list.comma() (by @​MahinAnowar).
  • Fixed whitespace-only values in list.space() (by @​MahinAnowar).
  • Fixed rule’s end position on space before semicolon (by @​maximilliangrand).
  • Fixed types (by @​romainmenke).
  • Fixed Chinese text in deprecation warning (by @​Jesse205).

8.5.26

  • Fixed list.split() regression (by @​lazerg).
  • Track symlinks in path protection in source map loading (by @​drengir1).

8.5.25

  • Fixed 8.5.17 visitor regression.
  • Fixed list.split() for non-string values (by @​amir-rezaei).

8.5.24

  • Preserve the BOM after the processing (by @​hdimer).

8.5.23

  • Do not load source map without opts.from for security reasons.

8.5.22

  • Fixed custom property losing semicolon before a comment (by @​sarathfrancis90).

8.5.21

  • Fixed childless at-rule losing semicolon before comment (by @​sarathfrancis90).
  • Fixed docs (by @​isker).

8.5.20

  • Fixed missing space if AtRule#params is set after (by @​sarathfrancis90).
  • Fixed mixing AST error on warnings (by @​MahinAnowar).

8.5.19

  • Fixed cleaning before for new nodes inserted to Root (by @​MahinAnowar).

8.5.18

  • Restricted loading previous source maps file to the opts.from folder for security reasons (use unsafeMap: true to disable the check).

8.5.17

  • Fixed Maximum call stack size exceeded error.
  • Fixed Prototype hijacking for postcss.fromJSON().
  • Fixed Input#origin() for unmapped end position (by @​chatman-media).

8.5.16

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
[grafana] Set hero chart ranges and filter early evaluations (#9120)

Start the hero-run MFU chart at 0%, with a soft maximum of 30%. Use soft
limits of 1.20–1.60 nats/token for train loss. Expand these ranges to
include extreme values instead of clipping samples to the 2nd–98th
percentiles.

Default Paloma loss to evaluations at or above 1% of the maximum
cumulative token count across all report samples. Add 10% of the
displayed loss span as padding at each end. This prevents initial
evaluations from compressing later changes. A Full run control restores
all sampled evaluations. Keep each run's color when the view changes.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[SFT Datakit] Add Pipeline to Normalize and Validate Chat Data (#9056)

A set of basic validations a la normalization for pretraining. Many SFT
datasets mix text and control tokens somewhat willy nilly, which makes
it easy to end up with lack of control or mis-formatted control tokens
in SFT.

1) Standardizes on [Harmony](https://github.com/openai/harmony) format
which handles normal chat templating + a cleaner format for reasoning,
tool calls, and tool responses.
2) Implements per source parsing and normalization for SFT data that is
indexed in datakit
3) Asserts that "normalized" chat data abides by the below contract to
avoid issues in downstream rendering

- Messages contain text only. This pipeline doesn’t support images,
audio, or other media.
- System and developer instructions come first. This separates the
initial instructions from the conversation.
- The conversation starts with a user request. The assistant needs
something to respond to.
- User messages cannot be blank or consecutive. Sources combine adjacent
user messages so each request forms one turn.
- Assistant messages cannot be blank and must identify reasoning,
commentary, or a final answer. This keeps those different kinds of
output distinguishable.
- After a final answer, the next message must be from the user. A final
answer marks the end of the assistant’s turn.
- Tool calls name a tool and provide arguments as a JSON object. This
makes the requested action explicit.
- Tool replies must match outstanding calls, in order. This connects
each result to the action that produced it.
- Outstanding tool calls must finish before the conversation resumes.
Otherwise, the assistant would continue without the expected results.
- Every called tool must have a definition. The model needs to know
which tools exist and how to call them in it's prompt or we are
incentivizing our model to hallucinate tools.
- Incorrect tool arguments are allowed. Failed attempts and corrections
can be useful training examples.
- Records end with the assistant, but may stop at reasoning or an
unanswered tool call. This supports training on incomplete attempts.

[ci] Include experiment tests in test selection (#9091)

Select tests in `experiments/` when those tests or modules they import
change. Include `experiments/` in the full Marin suite. The CI selector
previously searched only `tests/`, although the root pytest
configuration includes the two directories.

Ordinary experiment source changes continue to select tests through
module-scope imports. Changes to experiment `conftest.py` files or
non-Python files select the full Marin suite. Deleted experiment source
modules also select the full Marin suite because the current import
graph cannot identify their dependent tests. Existing marker exclusions
still apply.

commits.author: MaxFreedomPollard
commits.message:
[markdown] Omit the link and image title when the HTML has none (#8938)

Render an anchor or image with no `title` attribute as `[text](href)`
and `![alt](src)`. `convert_a` and `convert_img` built the title suffix
as `' "{title}"'.format(title=... if title else "")`, so the conditional
chose between the escaped title and an empty string inside the quotes
instead of choosing between the suffix and no suffix. markdownify
applies the conditional to the whole suffix, which is why its output
carries no trailing `""`.

The default `ResiliparseConfig` keeps links and images, so this reached
the web extraction path. Regenerating the fixtures with
`tests/snapshots/generate_expected.py` removes 161 empty titles over 106
lines in 8 of the 11 `tests/snapshots/web/expected/resiliparse` files
and changes nothing else. The wiki, ar5iv, stackexchange and dclm_hq
fixtures are unchanged because those configs set `include_links=False`
and `include_images=False`.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[zephyr] Compress Parquet output with zstd and page indexes (#8401)

Write Zephyr Parquet outputs with zstd level 3, page indexes, and at
most 256 rows per data page. Five local 2,000-row samples across
tokenize, dedup, normalized, embedding, and processed outputs were
28–50% smaller than Snappy.

On one 409,438,075-byte SVG tokenize shard, page indexes added 10,393
bytes (0.00384%) at the 256-row page cap. A 64-row cap increased the
complete file by 3.87%; 256 rows retained compression while providing
four times finer page-level pruning than 1,024 rows. An Iris canary
wrote 27 SVG tokenize shards from 11,086,947,772 to 7,314,765,643 bytes,
saving 3.51 GiB (34.0%) across 3,644,694 rows.

Query-read impact and sustained write throughput have not been
benchmarked.

Part of #8356

---------

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
[cleanup] Collapse duplicated helpers and drop a redundant query (#9106)

`marin.profiling` defined the XLA op-name canonicalization policy (strip
a
leading `%`, strip a trailing `.<digits>`) three times: the exported
`semantics.canonical_op_name`, `schema._canonical_name`, and
`trace_summary._canonical_name_part`. `trace_summary` imported the
shared helper
and kept its own copy alongside it, so `HotOp.canonical_name` and the
hierarchy/gap-label grouping could drift apart while deriving names from
the same
ops. Both private copies are gone and their call sites use the shared
helper,
which now carries the `@cache` that `_canonical_name_part` had.

The Iris controller's `_read_task_with_attempts` fetched its row through
`reads.get_task_detail`, which runs a second `GROUP BY` over
`task_attempts` to
derive per-task failure and preemption counts. `TaskWithAttempts` has no
count
fields; clients derive them from the attempt rows it carries. That
aggregate was
built and discarded on every `GetTaskStatus`, `KickTask`, `ProfileTask`,
`ExecInContainer`, and `GetProcessStatus` call. The read now uses
`reads.task_detail_query()` directly, the same statement the job-listing
and
federation-delta paths already use. `get_task_detail` is unchanged and
still
serves the callers that read the counts.

`levanter.data.utils.batched` reimplemented `itertools.batched`, which
Python
3.12 provides and which iris and marin already import from the standard
library.
The module is deleted and its call sites import the stdlib version.
`itertools.batched` yields tuples, so `stack_batches` and
`_BatchMappedShardedDataSource` build a list where they extend the batch
or pass
it to a `Callable[[list[T]], ...]`.

---------
